summary: Prefix cache backoff + aggressive eviction causing repeat-prompt p99 timeouts for customer LumenDocs
description: Issue summary: Customer LumenDocs reports higher-than-expected p99 latencies and occasional request timeouts for identical repeat prompts. Impact: Multiple customer API calls returning 504/timeouts and p99 token latency spikes ~2.5-3x baseline during short bursts of identical user messages. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, production traffic, model pinned to redwood/opt-6.9b. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send 500 concurrent identical prompts with 1024 token context, 2) Observe increased 504s and p99 generation latency for subsequent identical prompts. Expected behavior: Repeated identical prompts should hit prefix/KV cache and have low p99 (baseline ~450ms). Actual behavior: p99 spikes to 1.2s-1.6s and ~2% of requests return 504/timeouts during bursts.
reproduction_steps: Use customer's prompt template with 1024 token context
Run 500 concurrent identical requests against their dedicated endpoint over 30s
Monitor per-request cache hit/miss and generation latency metrics
logs_snippets: [2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] cache-manager WARN prefix-lookup backoff triggered for key=lk:prefix:abcd ttl=0.3s attempt=3
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] serving-runtime ERROR generation timeout request_id=xyz-43 504 elapsed=32000ms
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] cache-store INFO shard-evict evicted=128 reason=pressure target_shard=7
comments: Support (Maya): Customer reported p99 spikes coincide with scheduled marketing batch sending identical prompts. Asked for sample traffic and timestamps.
Customer (LumenDocs - Alex): Sent logs for 2026-03-10 14:00-14:05 UTC, reproduced with our internal load test.

SRE (Liam): Correlated spike to cache miss rate jump and increased eviction counts on customer's dedicated pool. Instituted temporary mitigation to reduce eviction aggressiveness and disabled prefix backoff for this pool.
Eng (Priya): Investigating possible lock contention in prefix lookup code path under high request fan-in. We see elevated mutex hold times in the prefix cache trie.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: cache hit rate dropped from 98% to 62% during the burst window; eviction rate increased ~7x.

Hypothesis: aggressive eviction + exponential backoff on prefix lookups causes upstream warmup storms when identical prompts reappear — clients experience cold misses and queueing in the serving runtime, amplifying p99.
Observed increased mutex contention in cache-shard allocation: avg hold time rose from 150us -> 1.2ms during peak.
Related past tickets: SUP-34121 and SUP-55321 showed similar prefix warmup patterns but not the same backoff/eviction coupling.
mitigation_applied: Rolled out temporary config to LumenDocs dedicated pool: increase prefix cache TTL from 300ms -> 3s
Disabled exponential backoff path for prefix lookups on that pool
Lowered eviction aggressiveness threshold to reduce thrashing
resolution: Mitigation reduced p99 and 504s immediately: after config change p99 returned to ~520ms and timeouts fell <0.1%. Root fix scheduled: change prefix cache locking to per-bucket optimistic reads and introduce adaptive TTL tuned to request fan-in.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-11 03:14 UTC; monitoring shows stable behavior. Engineering will land a non-breaking runtime change to reduce lock contention (PR referenced above) and a separate follow-up to add adaptive TTL controls. Customer success scheduled follow-up call 2026-03-13 to review change and request opt-in for adaptive caching when available.
